84909.name: Ken Jacobs

diagnosis.header: Ken explicitly stated disinterest in selling credits on 2024-05-29.
diagnosis.body: On 2024-05-29, the note records Ken's feedback: "Doing some sustainable actions, but not interested in selling credits." Despite this clarity, Ben sent four consecutive emails between 2025-12-05 and 2025-12-12 pitching ACCU revenue and carbon credit potential, culminating in a call on 2026-03-03 where Ken cited geography as the reason: "Outside the 2hr radius for Storm Boy."

diagnosis.header: Ignoring stated objection for 18 months created false warm signal.
diagnosis.body: Ken's core objection—not wanting to monetize carbon—was documented but overridden by a nurture campaign that treated him as a prospect to convert. The 2026-03-03 call cited logistics, not the underlying lack of appetite, masking the real issue: Ken was never a fit for AgriProve's core revenue model. Continuing contact after a documented "no" to credits burns credibility and wastes cycles on a prospect whose incentive structure differs from the rest of the portfolio.

diagnosis.header: Acknowledge his stated position and exit cleanly, not tentatively.
diagnosis.body: Ken told you on 2024-05-29 he is "not interested in selling credits." A "one last attempt" contradicts that boundary and risks him feeling pestered. The lever is honesty: confirm his preference hasn't changed, respect it if it hasn't, and move on. This preserves relationship equity if his situation changes later, rather than leaving him frustrated.

84909.next_step_short: Call Ken, confirm no-credits stance, close lead honestly
84909.next_step_qualifier: Ken explicitly declined credit sales on 2024-05-29. One transparent call to confirm that's still his position, then mark closed. Don't nurture or defer—respect his boundary.

Only then can the send-collateral decision be calibrated—not on elapsed time, but on Bill's stated readiness.

87901.next_step_qualifier: The visit log contains no outcome notes. Contact the farm visitor (Hobbs Magaret) immediately to capture what Bill said, asked for, or committed to on 2026-05-13, so the next step is based on actual feedback, not time elapsed.

The email asks Adam for data (lot numbers, paddock maps) rather than presenting terms, signaling AgriProve has not yet qualified Adam's readiness or internal process.

Post-farm-visit silence (especially >7 days) typically converts warm rural operators to cold, because they assume the vendor isn't serious or will circle back generically. The Yanko runs 6,000 Merino ewes on 12,000–13,000 ha (research note 2025-05-06)—a scale and cash-flow profile where soil-carbon sequestration and residual-income stacking matter, but only if re-engaged with specificity, not goodwill.

This gives Ian a concrete reason to open, reply, or call back—not a check-in asking "what did you think?" Generic follow-up will land in the void; artifact-led re-entry will provoke either a yes, a no, or a clarifying question.

324031758803.next_step_qualifier: Use The Yanko's 12,000 ha and 6,000 Merino ewes as the frame. Reference a peer property if available. Make it reply-worthy, not a check-in.
